roundShape: full round, as the architect set it. round-shape.py over my last verified head 3e191696 and this head 8526acee lists 3 files whose own diff differs: loadtest/README.md, loadtest/cluster/cluster.sh and loadtest/cluster/cluster.test.sh. cluster.sh's change is the copy_is_ours guard on every stop, kill, write and remove path in the run path, so the real surface was driven again: two live runs, below.

implementerProof.how: Driven, not read. The live check the architect asked for ran on the free namespace: run A (lt-20261030t220008-b75e) up, seed, `step killed 1 --duration 5m`; its step shell killed with SIGKILL at 22:19:48Z, so no EXIT trap ran; its two surviving children (the disk watcher and the runner-job wait) both ended by 22:21:35Z, logging `step killed: the step that started this disk watcher is gone; it stops, recording nothing and stopping no job` and `job step-killed: the step that started this wait is gone; the wait ends, stopping no job`, and the runner job step-killed kept running with no .rc file, stopped by nothing. Then run A was downed and run B (lt-20261030t222320-55aa) took the lock and ran a step of THE SAME NAME, `killed`: it completed its full 120 s window at 4.00 events/s committed with 7,243 of 7,243 requests 2xx, every file present including pg-disk.json and heap.txt, and no step-failed.json - nothing of run A stopped, removed or marked anything of run B. Those two runs also exercise the new guards on the normal path: 19 copy_is_ours call sites now sit in up, seed, reset, step and down, and both runs passed through them end to end. The audit table of issuecomment-6534359964 I walked against the source myself rather than reading it; one omission is named in failures-free note below. cluster.test.sh gives 49 PASS, 0 FAIL at this head; against 7604610d's cluster.sh the same suite fails, see the proof's negative control.

notes: The audit table, walked against the source: every path that stops, kills, deletes or removes in a shared pod is in it and the guard it names is there - scale_to :1298, runner_put :1430, runner_start :1461, runner_stop :1476, runner_wait's deadline stop through runner_stop, typing_stop :2187 and :2191, runner_step_remove :2374, the replay dump's two rm paths :2765 and :2773, run_replay's rm -rf :2898, pg_disk_watch :1255, and the reachability guards the table claims for the drops and the NATS purge hold (reset_copy calls stop_copy before `drop database dispatch` at :1405 and nats_purge at :1413; replay-prepare the same at :2747 before :2749, :2750 and :2785). One path is MISSING from the table: apply_manifest (:575), which writes the shared fixed-name objects (the dispatch and listener deployments, the postgres StatefulSet, nats, secrets) and carries no copy_is_ours of its own. Its three callers are each covered by something else - up :3206-3210 runs immediately after kube_lock_take, which fails when another run holds the lock; resize_postgres :2617 and cmd_redeploy both call stop_copy or scale_to first, whose guard dies - so I found no behaviour gap, and I am naming it as an audit omission rather than a defect: a reader checking the table against the source will find a write path the table does not list.

CI is unread at the code head f7beb833, which the architect asked me to name: at 22:42Z lint, typecheck, test and envoy-go were all queued, and pr-title has one cancelled and one successful run. The reviewer must read all five there. What I ran in the workspace is not CI's answer.

Cases (x) and (y) were not shown red at 7604610d by me: the suite stops at its first failure, so one control run shows (w) red and never reaches them. What I can state instead is structural and stronger for the whole class: copy_is_ours does not exist at 7604610d, so every path the table lists was unguarded there.
